items.title: Section: Abiding in Benefiting Beings Opens — Being a Genuine Companion

items.zh: 又諸菩薩由十一相，名住一切種饒益有情戒。於一一相中成就一切種。謂諸菩薩，於諸有情彼彼事業，皆為助伴。謂於思量所作事業，及於功用所作事業，悉能與彼而作助伴。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, through eleven aspects, are said to abide in discipline benefiting beings in its every kind. Bodhisattvas become a genuine companion in whatever endeavour beings are engaged in — whether an endeavour arising from careful deliberation or one carried out through active effort, they are able to become a companion in either.

items.zh: 或於道路若往、若來，或於無倒事業加行，或於守護所有財物，或於和合展轉乖離，或於義會，或於修福，皆為助伴。
items.en: Whether accompanying them on a journey, correcting a distorted approach to some task, protecting their property, reconciling a broken relationship, joining a genuinely meaningful gathering, or supporting an act of merit — one becomes a companion in all of these.

items.title: Section: Rescuing From Every Kind of Affliction — Disaster and the Five Hindrances

items.zh: 於諸救苦亦為助伴。謂於遭遇疾疫有情瞻侍供給，盲者啟導，聾者撝義，手代言者曉以想像，迷方路者示以遇途，支不具者惠以荷乘，其愚騃者誨以勝慧。
items.en: One also becomes a companion in rescuing beings from suffering: attending and providing for those afflicted by illness or epidemic; guiding the blind; opening up meaning for the deaf; making oneself understood to those who speak by hand-gesture; showing the way to a traveller lost in an unfamiliar place; providing transport for those with a physical disability; and teaching genuine wisdom to those of simple understanding.

items.zh: 為貪欲纏所苦有情，開解令離貪欲纏苦。如是若為瞋恚、惛沈睡眠、掉舉惡作、疑纏所苦有情，開解令離疑纏等苦。
items.en: Towards beings suffering under the grip of craving, one explains and resolves it, freeing them from that suffering. In the same way, towards those suffering under aversion, torpor and drowsiness, restlessness and worry, or doubt, one explains and resolves each, freeing them from that suffering.

items.title: Eight Kinds of Unwholesome Thought, the Sting of Comparison, and Simple Travel Fatigue

items.zh: 欲尋思纏所苦有情，開解令離欲尋思苦。如欲尋思，恚、害、親里、國土、不死、輕侮相應、族姓相應所有尋思，當知亦爾。
items.en: Towards beings troubled by desire-oriented discursive thought, one explains and resolves it, freeing them from that suffering. As with desire-oriented thought, so too with thoughts of hostility, harm, homeland, family, denial of mortality, contempt and comparison, and the standing of patron families.

items.zh: 他蔑、他勝所苦有情，開解令離被蔑、勝苦。行路疲乏所苦有情，施座施處，調身按摩，令其止息勞倦眾苦。
items.en: Towards beings suffering from being belittled or overpowered by another, one explains and resolves it, freeing them from that suffering. Towards beings suffering exhaustion from travel, one offers a seat and a place to rest, adjusting and massaging the body, so that their weariness is genuinely eased.

items.title: Section: Teaching Each According to Need — Principled and Accommodating Speech

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，為諸有情如理宣說。謂於樂行惡行有情，為欲令斷諸惡行故，以相應文句、助伴、隨順、清亮、有用、相稱、應順、常委分資糧法而為宣說。或復方便善巧宣說。
items.en: Bodhisattvas teach beings in accordance with genuine principle. Towards beings inclined to wrongdoing, in order to bring that wrongdoing to an end, they teach using coherent language, mutually supporting points, a natural progression, clarity, genuine usefulness, fitting relevance, timeliness, and the sustained, thorough presentation of the very qualities that support the path — or, alternatively, they teach through skilful accommodation instead.

items.zh: 如於樂行惡行有情，為欲令斷諸惡行故；如是於行慳行，有情為欲令彼斷慳行故；於現法中求財寶者，為欲令彼正少功力，集多財寶，守護無失；於佛聖教懷憎嫉者，為欲令彼得清淨信，證清淨見，超諸惡趣，盡一切結，越一切苦；應知亦爾。
items.en: Just as with beings inclined to wrongdoing, so too with beings inclined to stinginess, taught so as to end that stinginess; with beings presently seeking wealth, taught so that, with only a little effort, they gather abundant wealth and keep it safe; and with beings who resent or feel hostility towards the Buddha's teaching, taught so that they attain pure faith, realise a pure view, rise above the miserable realms, and ultimately exhaust every fetter and cross beyond all suffering.

items.title: Section: Knowing and Repaying Kindness — Warm Welcome, Generous Repayment, Unbidden Help

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於其有恩諸有情所深知恩惠，常思酬報。暫見申敬，讚言善來，怡顏歡慰，吐誠談謔；祥處設座，正筵令坐。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards anyone who has shown them kindness, genuinely recognise that debt and constantly consider how to repay it. ... The moment they see such a person, they show genuine respect, exclaiming warmly, "how wonderful that you have come," greeting them with a cheerful expression and sincere, easy conversation, offering a fitting place and a properly arranged seat.

items.zh: 若等若增財利供養現前酬答，非以下劣。於彼事業雖不求請，尚應伴助。況于有命。
items.en: They repay in person with material support equal to or greater than what was given, never with something lesser. Towards that benefactor's own endeavours, even without being asked, they should still help — how much more so, then, when actually asked.

items.zh: 如於事業，如是於苦，於如理說，於方便說，於濟怖畏，於衰惱處開解愁憂，於惠資具，於與依止，於隨心轉，於顯實德令深歡悅，於懷親愛方便調伏，於現神通驚恐引攝，如應廣說，當知亦爾。

items.title: Section: Rescuing From Every Kind of Fear

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於遭怖畏諸有情類，能為救護。謂於種種禽獸、水火、王賊、怨敵、家主、宰官、不活、惡名、大眾、威德、非人、起屍、魍魎等畏，皆能救護，令得安隱。
items.en: Bodhisattvas are able to rescue beings caught in fear — fear of predatory animals, of flood and fire, of oppressive rulers and bandits, of enemies, of a domineering household head, of corrupt officials, fear of not surviving, of a ruined reputation, of a crowd, of being overwhelmed by authority, and fear of non-human beings, reanimated corpses, or malevolent spirits — rescuing beings from all of these, restoring their peace of mind.

items.title: Section: Resolving Grief Over Lost Family and Lost Wealth

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於處衰惱諸有情類，能善開解，令離愁憂。或依親屬有所衰亡。所謂父母、兄弟、妻子、奴婢、僮僕、宗長、朋友、內外族因、親教、軌範及餘尊重，時有喪亡，善為開解，令離憂惱。
items.en: Bodhisattvas are able to skilfully comfort beings genuinely grieving, freeing them from sorrow. Whether grieving the loss of family — parents, siblings, spouse, household staff, elders, friends, extended relatives, one's own preceptor, instructing teacher, or other respected figures — they skilfully comfort them, freeing them from grief.

items.zh: 或依財寶有所喪失。謂或王賊之所侵奪，或火所燒，或水所溺，或為矯詐之所誑誘，或由事業無方損失，或為惡親非理橫取，或家生火之所耗費，於如是等財寶喪失，善為開解，令離憂惱。由是因緣，諸有情類生軟中上三品愁憂，菩薩皆能正為開解。
items.en: Or grieving the loss of wealth — seized by rulers or bandits, burned by fire, swept away by flood, lost to deception, lost through a poorly managed enterprise, wrongfully seized by a predatory relative, or drained away by the "household fire" of a spendthrift heir or the household's own internal strife — they skilfully comfort them, freeing them from grief. Whatever the resulting grief's degree, mild, moderate, or severe, bodhisattvas are able to rightly comfort it.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，備資生具，隨有來求，即皆施與。謂諸有情求食與食，求飲與飲，求乘與乘，求衣與衣，求莊嚴具施莊嚴具，求諸什物施以什物，求鬘塗香施鬘塗香，求止憩處施止憩處，求諸光明施以光明。
items.en: Bodhisattvas keep life's necessities ready, giving them the moment they are requested: food for one seeking food, drink for one seeking drink, transport, clothing, ornaments, everyday goods, perfume and garlands, lodging, or light, each given exactly as requested.

blocks.text: What the eleven ways of benefiting beings look like in practice. Much of this would be at home in a modern guide to social service.

In "whatever endeavour beings are engaged in, whether arising from deliberation or active effort", the bodhisattva helps: "accompanying them on a journey, correcting a distorted approach, protecting their property, reconciling a broken relationship, joining a meaningful gathering". Master Cháng Bǎi: three kinds of volition: deliberating, deciding, initiating.

"Attending the sick; guiding the blind; opening up meaning for the deaf; being hands and feet for those without." Helping beings troubled by each hindrance and by the eight unwholesome thoughts; those "belittled or overpowered by another"; those "exhausted from travel", by offering a seat and rest.
To the wrongdoer, teaching "so as to end the wrongdoing"; to the stingy, "so as to end stinginess"; to one seeking wealth, how to gain it with little effort and lawfully.
"The moment they see such a person, they show genuine respect" (Master Cháng Bǎi: "You've come at just the right time, welcome!"); they repay "equal or greater" than received, and help even unasked.
From predatory animals, flood and fire, rulers and bandits, enemies, a domineering household head, corrupt officials. Master Cháng Bǎi adds social fear: feeling inferior in a crowd.

For those who lost family ("parents, siblings, spouse, friends"), or wealth ("seized by rulers or bandits, burned, swept away, lost through deception or a failed enterprise"). Venerable Miào Jìng: a spendthrift in the family ruins it.
"Kept ready, given the moment they are requested."

quiz.q: In which two kinds of endeavour does the treatise say bodhisattvas can be a companion to beings?
options: endeavours arising from deliberation and those carried out through active effort
quiz.why: "Whether an endeavour arising from careful deliberation or one carried out through active effort, they are able to become a companion in either." Master Cháng Bǎi: what is done by the mind is called "done through deliberation."

quiz.q: Explaining "endeavours arising from deliberation," what three kinds of volition does Master Cháng Bǎi name?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: there are three kinds of volition — deliberating, deciding, and initiating.

quiz.q: "Huī yì for the deaf" is rendered "communicating meaning to the deaf." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: "huī" means to reveal — revealing principles to them so their wisdom grows
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "huī" means to reveal; "huī yì" is revealing principles to them so that their wisdom grows. The English stops at "communicating meaning."

quiz.q: Among the eight unwholesome thoughts, "thought connected with family lineage" is rendered "social standing." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: with a defiled mind, clinging to patrons and frequenting powerful households
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with a defiled mind, clinging to patrons and going back and forth to powerful households. The English "social standing" misses this sense.

quiz.q: Towards a benefactor, "the moment they see them, they show respect, exclaiming 'welcome.'" How does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate this?
options: "Oh, you've come at just the right time — welcome!"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Oh, you've come at just the right time — welcome!" He glosses "xuè" as cheerful joking. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the moment they see" means paying respect as soon as they meet — really an expression of thanks.

quiz.q: Which of these are among the fears the treatise says bodhisattvas can rescue beings from?
options: fear of not surviving, of a ruined reputation, of a crowd
quiz.why: The list includes fear of predatory animals, flood and fire, rulers and bandits, enemies, household heads, officials, not surviving, a ruined reputation, crowds, authority, non-humans, reanimated corpses, and goblins. Venerable Miào Jìng: "not surviving" means life is so hard one cannot go on.

quiz.q: One cause of lost wealth is "jiā shēng huǒ," rendered "a household's own internal strife." How do the lectures explain it?
options: Miào Jìng: a wastrel in the family ruins it; Cháng Bǎi: either a wastrel squanders the wealth, or the family quarrels among itself
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a spendthrift in your family ruins you. Master Cháng Bǎi gives two readings: a wastrel uses up the family fortune, or spouses, parents and children, or siblings quarrel. The English takes only the second.
